author: askalphaxiv
text:
"Multi-Stream Attention Residuals"

An alternative to mHC and AttentionRes?

Standard residual connections combine information from all previous Transformer layers into one hidden state, making earlier information harder to access as models get deeper.

Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR) lets each Transformer layer retrieve information from earlier layers using multiple attention heads, with each head looking at a different range of previous tokens to decide which information to retrieve.

MSAR outperforms standard residuals, mHC, and AttnRes across all 12 benchmarks, achieving a 1.58x iso-loss training FLOP efficiency improvement over standard residuals based on fitted scaling laws, while adding just 0.5% training FLOPs per step.

https://alphaxiv.org/abs/2610.13630

author: mathemetica
text:
Four equations. The complete map of physical reality.

Schrödinger’s equation tracks how a quantum wave function evolves in time under the Hamiltonian. Maxwell’s equations link electric and magnetic fields to charge, current, and light. 
Einstein’s field equation equates spacetime curvature to the stress-energy tensor of matter. Dirac’s equation unifies quantum mechanics with special relativity for spin-1/2 particles and predicts antimatter.

They remain the sharpest language we have for how the universe actually works.

author: LensScientific
text:
Smooth flow and chaotic flow can involve the same fluid.

Reynolds number Re = ρvL/μ compares inertia with viscosity. Low values favor orderly layers; high values make disturbances harder to damp and turbulence more likely. Geometry and roughness help determine the transition.

author: 0xDevShah
text:
Introducing Optimus-1, the first swarm harness for autonomous research. Generally available in ArkenOS, starting now.

Optimus-1 lets ArkenOS spawn a swarm that runs the entire discovery loop on hard research problems autonomously. The harness samples the hypothesis space in parallel and works the tails of the distribution, chasing every anomaly until it resolves into an artifact or a discovery. We want every researcher to have a lab of their own, and to see how far their curiosity can go.

Unlike coding agents, Optimus-1 is designed for long-horizon discovery, where most branches fail, and the hard part is knowing which result to believe. It keeps what replicates and keeps pushing past the edge of what's known.

We're still early, but ArkenOS is helping hundreds of teams, from RL environments and data labs to frontier research groups, scale the alpha in their core research.

If you're working on a hard research problem and want to try it, my DMs are open. I'd love to hear what you'd point it at.
